biography.plain_text: William Robert Shields, known as Bill, is an American plastics businessman based in Yakima, Washington. He founded Rainier Plastics, which reprocesses industrial scrap, and owned his family's Shields Bag and Printing business. The packaging company became part of Novolex in 2018; he retained his separate role as Rainier's owner and chairman.

long_biography.plain_text:
A dinner conversation drew plastics businessman Bill Shields into endurance rallying. When a friend mentioned the Peking to Paris event, he immediately agreed to join him; two days later, he had found a car. The pair drove a vintage Dodge across the route, recovering from a suspension failure to finish. Shields later took a Chevrolet through the demanding terrain between Buenos Aires and Cape Horn.

His interest in the outdoors also includes land conservation. Brought up to regard care for the land as a responsibility, he has supported Washington's shrub-steppe habitat. He has also worked with the Yakama Nation on wildlife projects, including the reintroduction of antelope.

confidence.reason: Full specialist interview supplies dinner decision, repair setback and later rally; primary board profile supports conservation activity without attributing sole responsibility.
